MANILA, Philippines – The Senate has realigned nearly P20 billion from government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance Program (MAP) and the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS), to augment funding for the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) under the proposed 2027 national budget.

Senator JV Ejercito, chairperson of the Senate finance committee, said on Wednesday, November 25, that the P19.8-billion realignment would help increase PhilHealth’s allocation from P73 billion in the House version of the General Appropriations Bill (GAB) to P94.2 billion in the Senate version of the budget measure.
PhilHealth subsidies in the national budget cover the premium contributions of vulnerable sectors that cannot afford to pay their own health insurance premiums.

“Our target is to increase PhilHealth subsidy to P100 billion but we have a tight fiscal space. Hopefully, we can reach our target so PhilHealth can have better subsidies,” Ejercito told reporters in a mix of English and Filipino.
Of the P19.8 billion, P9.9 billion was realigned from MAP funds and another P9.9 billion from AICS.

Ejercito said the funds would go directly to hospitals to support the implementation of the Zero Balance Billing (ZBB) program. This includes P7.6 billion for Department of Health (DOH) hospitals, P2 billion for legacy hospitals, and P1 billion for local government unit (LGU) hospitals.

The Senate also provided an additional P5.49 billion for the Hospital Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP), P1.099 billion for health promotion, P1.599 billion for immunization programs, and P736 million for the Sulu Transition Program.

Ejercito also addressed concerns raised by Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson over possible duplicate funding for infrastructure projects, including multi-purpose buildings (MPBs), under the proposed 2027 national budget.

“If we saw red flags, including double entries in the GAB, definitely, we’ll remove that. But of course, it is not humanly possible to check everything at once. That’s thousands of entries, so we need to check it slowly,” Ejercito said.

He acknowledged that some questionable entries might have escaped the committee’s scrutiny, but said this was not intentional. He also called on budget watchdogs to help identify possible irregularities.

“If some entries have been let out of our sight, that’s not intentional. So we’re seeking everyone’s help, including budget watchdogs, to tell us if they observe some red flags. If we found that it has basis, we’ll definitely remove the items,” Ejercito added.

The Senate began plenary deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for fiscal year 2027 on Monday, November 23. Lacson, ahead of the deliberations, flagged alleged double and triple appropriations for some flood control projects in the GAB, saying some of them had already received funding in previous years. – Rappler.com
